original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum. Report the word's packing cap from ceiling.ceiling() and the fraction of it realized; label packing gains as such.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

existing_checks.scope: Packing-independent ceiling for the selected paid profile under the one-unpaid-coordinate coverage and halving guard.
existing_checks.remaining: A changed word or model requires new pricing; a local packing search must name uncovered scope.

actual_scope: Determine what the per-call versus pooled per-replica accounting unit does to the selected complex word's packing ceiling: convert PR #1685's proved integer optimum into the ceiling it implies, and test whether the two-unpaid-coordinates lever is integrality-forbidden only because the incumbent prices one call.
scope_change_reason: The card's first experiment, a new named packing search, was duplicative: PR #1685 had already proved the unrestricted integer idle optimum for this exact word and PR #3729 had already produced the per-call integrality ceiling. The unexamined quantity was neither optimum nor per-call ceiling but the accounting unit itself. Pooling is the model #1685 uses and the model the incumbent does not, and it changes both the baseline ceiling and the admissibility of a published lever premise.
bottleneck_link: The binding complex side's screening numbers depend on an unstated accounting choice worth 0.085 percent in a, and it decides whether a lever premise already published in levers.py is admissible at all. Correct screening saves effort on the binding side even though no frontier value changes.
stop_rule: Certify the pooled ceiling as a two-sided rational interval, reproduce #1685's published optimum as a cross-check, certify the per-call versus pooled integrality split for unpaid=2 at three pooling levels, and stop without any supplier, realisability or frontier claim.
evidence: README.md proofs, model table and scope; RESULT.json exact brackets, the three pooling levels for unpaid=2 and control counts; verify.py registered replay with a deliberate-failure mutation checked by the author.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Is the accounting unit per call or per replica in the selected contract?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It changes the baseline packing ceiling by 0.085 percent in a and decides whether the two-unpaid-coordinates premise is admissible at all.
open_questions.first_step: Read the PR1012 coverage identity's statement on whether the centre charge and the unpaid coordinate attach per call or per replica, then reconcile the incumbent's w = families/stages convention with #1685's W = 14336, N = 144.
open_questions.blocked_by: A documentation and contract decision. The arithmetic of both models is already certified here; neither source settles which one is binding.

open_questions.question: What ceiling survives owner and hosting legality on the idle partition?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only route to a materially tighter bound. The unrestricted pooled optimum needs 4648 idle children per replica against 492 hosted helpers.
open_questions.first_step: Take one owner-family residual instance from the selected word and enumerate only legal partitions while holding the full local invoice fixed.
open_questions.blocked_by: No source-bound characterisation of legal idle groups and shared hosting resources exists. This is PR #1685's own stated next question and is not answered here.
